entries.matter: Skild's new robot model was built using NVIDIA infrastructure
source_spans: Skild AI’s new S1 robot foundation model helps address this, designed to learn previously unseen, long-horizon tasks from a single video demonstration. The model, launched last week, uses video as input to understand and execute the task without updating its weights or undergoing task-specific post-training — a technique called in-context learning.

Skild built S1 and conducted the research on NVIDIA AI infrastructure, part of a broader collaboration spanning synthetic data generation, model training, simulation and real-world physical AI deployment.
entries.source_speaker: NVIDIA blog; original confirmation source not specified
entries.meaning: A named robotics company used NVIDIA infrastructure to build and research a newly launched model. This is a concrete example of adoption in physical AI, but the article gives no NVIDIA revenue or usage amount.
entries.standard_boundary: v5 §5.1–5.2: named customer adoption can be evidence without an amount; §6: a small or unquantified customer action is supporting; §5.5: reported launch or completed action

entries.matter: Skild's commercial activity provides context for demand for NVIDIA's robotics infrastructure
source_spans: The launch comes as the company reached a $100 million annual revenue run rate 10 months after its first commercial deployment. In that time, Skild has built more than 60 deployment partnerships with work spanning manufacturing, logistics, inspection, security, food preparation and other applications.
entries.source_speaker: NVIDIA blog; original confirmation source not specified
entries.meaning: Article reports Skild reached a $100 million annual revenue run rate and more than 60 deployment partnerships. These are Skild figures, not NVIDIA revenue; a possible link to NVIDIA infrastructure demand is an inference, not a reported order.
entries.standard_boundary: v5 §5.1 and §5.3: another company's figures require a concrete demand connection; §6: another company's operating figures are supporting; §5.4: preserve the metric and its owner

entries.matter: Skild, NVIDIA and Foxconn are deploying robots to assemble NVIDIA Blackwell systems
source_spans: Skild, NVIDIA and Foxconn are deploying the Skild Brain on dual-arm manipulators for high-precision assembly of NVIDIA Blackwell systems. In one demonstrated workflow, a robot installs a busbar and limit block, fastens 16 screws and adapts to disturbances across a multistep task.
entries.source_speaker: NVIDIA blog; reporting ongoing deployment, completion and scale not established
entries.meaning: The named companies are deploying robotics in an NVIDIA system assembly workflow. This is a concrete deployment, but the article does not establish its scale, completion or financial effect.
entries.standard_boundary: v5 §5.1–5.2: named partner deployment is not discarded as a product detail; §5.4: preserve the ongoing status; §6: unquantified deployment is supporting

entries.matter: NVIDIA and Skild plan to make jointly developed simulation solvers available to all developers
source_spans: Skild and NVIDIA are also jointly developing new GPU-accelerated simulation solvers that quickly and accurately model how robots physically touch, grip and manipulate solid objects. They’ll soon be made available to all developers as part of Newton.
entries.source_speaker: NVIDIA blog announcing joint development and a planned release; no individual speaker named
entries.meaning: The jointly developed solvers are planned to become available to all developers; the text does not establish release has occurred or development began recently.
entries.standard_boundary: v5 §5.1–5.2: named partner action and an incomplete future step can be kept; §5.4–5.5: preserve planned release alongside the reported development; §6: supporting without demonstrated company-scale effect

salient_exclusions.source_span: In Skild’s tests on new, multistep tasks, its S1 robot succeeded about 66% of the time at each step, compared with 9% for a similar AI system — a more than sevenfold improvement. Skild also estimates that showing the robot one short video example can be as useful as giving it roughly 380 hands-on training examples. A person collecting those examples manually could take 50-100 hours.
salient_exclusions.reason: Skild's own product comparison and technical estimates are product details. They do not independently establish NVIDIA's commercial benefit.
salient_exclusions.standard_boundary: v5 §5.3 and D250 boundary 3: company or partner product comparisons are excluded
